decision.explanation: The provided evidence from pmid-27283860 directly supports the claim. The study is a phase 2 trial evaluating the combination of dabrafenib and trametinib in patients with previously treated metastatic BRAF V600E-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The results demonstrate an investigator-assessed confirmed overall response rate of 63.2% (36 of 57 patients), which provides direct evidence that this combination therapy supports sensitivity/response in this specific molecular and disease context. The BRAF V600E variant is somatically acquired in NSCLC, consistent with the query. The therapies and their interaction type (combination) are correctly identified. No revisions are needed as the evidence aligns perfectly with the claim's parameters.

citations.quote: In this phase 2, multicenter, nonrandomized, open-label study of patients with pretreated metastatic BRAF V600E-mutant NSCLC, antitumor activity and safety of oral dabrafenib (150 mg twice daily) plus oral trametinib (2 mg once daily) were evaluated. . . . With a median follow-up of 11.6 months (IQR 8.8-15.2), the investigator-assessed confirmed overall response was 63.2% (36 of 57; 95% CI 49.3-75.6), including 2 (3.5%) of 57 patients with CR and 34 (59.6%) of 57 with PR.
